title: How the day ended
text: Stocks rose again on Tuesday. The S&P 500 fund SPY closed at $769.71, up 0.6%, and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ closed at $721.21, up 1.3%. Tech led the way, and chip companies had a strong day. Tomorrow the Federal Reserve shares its interest rate decision at 2:00 PM Eastern time, so watch how stocks react. This is for learning, not advice.

title: Fed decision comes tomorrow
text: The Federal Reserve, the group that sets the main interest rate, meets October 27 and 28 and shares its decision on Wednesday at 2:00 PM Eastern time. Interest rates are the price of borrowing money, so they touch almost every stock. Growth companies like the AI names often move the most when the news surprises people. Expect a bumpy afternoon.

title: AMD and Rocket Lab jump, with big swings
text: AMD closed at $560.26, up 5.5%, and Rocket Lab closed at $58.31, up 8.3%. Both have a high beta (2.45 and 2.61). Beta tells us how much a stock usually moves compared with the whole market, and 1.0 means it moves about the same. A beta above 2 means bigger jumps up and bigger drops down. Rocket Lab is still far below its 52 week high of $151.00. We could not confirm what caused either move.

title: Meta and Lockheed give back some ground
text: Meta fell 1.6% to $620.19, and Lockheed Martin fell 1.9% to $622.99 after its big jump on Monday. Lockheed has a very low beta of 0.10, so it usually moves less than the market. A stock that jumps one day often settles back the next. One day tells us little, so it helps to look at longer stretches of time.

title: Broadcom rises on AI financing reports
text: Broadcom closed at $342.33, up 4.0%. News outlets have reported that Broadcom is in talks to raise more than $60 billion in debt to pay for AI chips used by Anthropic and others. These are reports of talks, not a finished deal. It shows how much money is flowing into the equipment behind AI.

title: Lesson 25: What is rebalancing?
text: Rebalancing means resetting your mix of investments back to the plan you chose. Say your plan is half in a stock fund and half in a bond fund. After stocks have a great year, the stock part might grow to 70% of your money. That is riskier than you planned. Rebalancing means moving some money back toward 50/50. It keeps your risk close to what you meant it to be. Some people rebalance once a year, or when the mix drifts a lot. It can feel odd to trim what is winning, but the goal is steady risk, not chasing the best performer. This is for learning, not advice to buy or sell anything.

title: What this board covers
text: This board follows 17 funds and companies in five groups: base ETFs, AI giants, AI suppliers, aerospace and space, and health. Prices and analyst targets come from FMP. Targets are missing for some companies because the free data plan does not include them. The risk score is our own simple estimate from 1 to 10, not a rating from any expert. Everything here is for learning, not advice to buy or sell.
